roadmap.title: Modern Angular Core
roadmap.goal: Build production-ready Angular applications using standalone architecture and modern template APIs.

topics.title: Angular Architecture & Standalone Components
hands: Create a standalone Angular app with feature folders.
Build reusable components without NgModule-centric architecture.
interview: Why are standalone components useful for lazy loading and tree-shaking?

topics.title: Components, Templates & Communication
theory: Signal-based inputs and modern component communication
hands: Build a reusable data table and modal.
Create parent-child communication and content projection examples.
interview: Why is track important for large lists?

topics.title: Directives & Pipes
hands: Build appPermission, appAutoFocus and appDebounceClick.
Create a pure custom pipe and demonstrate an impure-pipe performance issue.
interview: Why can an impure pipe be expensive?

topics.title: Dependency Injection
theory: Dependency Injection and inversion of control
hands: Create a configurable API service using InjectionToken.
Demonstrate root and component-level provider scope.
interview: How does Angular DI hierarchy work?
When would you use an InjectionToken?

topics.title: Routing, Guards, Resolvers & Lazy Loading
hands: Build /auth, /dashboard, /users/:id and /settings.
Implement role-based route protection and lazy-loaded features.
interview: How does lazy loading improve the initial bundle?
When should a resolver be avoided?

topics.title: Forms — Template-driven vs Reactive
theory: Signal Forms as a modern/experimental direction in Angular versions that support them
hands: Build a dynamic form from JSON.
Implement cross-field validation and a FormArray of addresses.
interview: How would you design a JSON-driven dynamic form?

roadmap.title: Advanced Angular & State Management
roadmap.goal: Master RxJS, Signals, change detection, authentication flows and scalable state architecture.

topics.title: RxJS Observables & Subjects
hands: Create a service exposing readonly state.
Refactor manual subscriptions to AsyncPipe or takeUntilDestroyed.
interview: How do you prevent subscription leaks?

topics.title: RxJS Operators — The Interview Core
theory: Transformation: map, switchMap, mergeMap, concatMap, exhaustMap
hands: Build typeahead search with cancellation.
Implement independent dashboard API loading and per-widget errors.
interview: switchMap vs mergeMap vs concatMap vs exhaustMap?
Why can switchMap be dangerous for writes?

topics.title: Angular Signals
theory: Signals for local and UI state
hands: Convert a BehaviorSubject-based local state service to Signals.
Build a filterable dashboard using signals and computed state.
interview: When should you not replace an Observable with a Signal?
What is computed() for? What should effects be used for?

topics.title: Change Detection, OnPush & Zoneless Concepts
theory: Zoneless Angular concepts in modern versions
hands: Diagnose unnecessary rendering in a large table.
Optimize a component tree with OnPush and reactive state.
interview: Why is a component rendering repeatedly?
What changes when Angular runs without Zone.js?

topics.title: HTTP Client, Interceptors & JWT Refresh
topics.code:
Request
  ↓
Interceptor
  ↓
401?
  ↓
Single refresh operation
  ↓
Retry pending requests
hands: Build login + access token + refresh token flow.
Handle five simultaneous 401 responses without triggering five refresh calls.
interview: How do you prevent concurrent refresh-token calls?
Where should authorization decisions ultimately be enforced?

topics.title: State Management & Facade Architecture
hands: Create a UsersFacade with loading, data and error state.
Document why a feature does or does not need a global store.
interview: How do you avoid a giant global state?

topics.title: Modern Angular: @defer, SSR/Hydration, AI Tooling
theory: Angular CLI AI/MCP tooling where supported by the target version
Accessibility primitives and modern Angular tooling
hands: Defer a heavy chart and compare loading behavior.
Explore the Angular CLI MCP workflow in a version that supports it.
interview: How can AI/MCP tooling help an Angular team without replacing engineering judgment?

roadmap.title: Tooling, Testing & Performance
roadmap.goal: Learn to ship, test, measure and optimize production Angular applications.

topics.title: Angular CLI & Build Tooling
theory: ng new, generate, serve, build, test, lint
ESBuild, tree shaking, code splitting, source maps
hands: Create production and development build configurations.
Inspect generated bundles and identify a large dependency.
interview: What does a bundler actually do?

topics.title: Unit Testing with Jest / Jasmine & Modern Test Runners
theory: Vitest in modern Angular setups where applicable
hands: Test login service, guard, interceptor, reactive form and component behavior.
Mock HTTP responses and test success/error paths.
interview: How do modern Angular projects choose a test runner?

topics.title: Angular Testing Library & Behavior-focused Testing
hands: Test a login form from the user's perspective.
Test loading, success, empty and error states.
interview: Why test behavior instead of private component variables?
How would you test accessibility-related behavior?

topics.title: Core Web Vitals & Browser Performance
hands: Measure a dashboard before and after optimization.
Find a slow interaction and identify its main-thread cause.
interview: How do you investigate poor INP?

topics.title: Angular Performance Optimization
hands: Optimize a 10,000-row table.
Reduce duplicate API calls in a dashboard and document before/after behavior.
interview: A table with 10,000 records is slow — what do you check first?
How do you identify a memory leak?

topics.title: Accessibility & Production Quality
hands: Make a modal keyboard accessible.
Audit a form and data table for keyboard and screen-reader usability.
interview: How do you preserve focus after navigation or modal interactions?

roadmap.title: Interview Preparation & Practical Assessment
roadmap.goal: Turn knowledge into interview performance: conceptual answers, coding, debugging, system design and project storytelling.

topics.title: Top Angular Conceptual Questions
hands: Practice 30 Angular questions without notes.
For every answer include definition → example → trade-off.
interview: How do you handle JWT refresh concurrency?

topics.title: Live Coding & Scenario Assessment
theory: Frontend coding differs from algorithm-only coding: prioritize correctness, state, UX, error handling and maintainability.
Practice incremental implementation and explain decisions while coding.
hands: Debounced search
Dynamic reactive form
Paginated/filterable table
Permission directive
Reusable modal
Dashboard with independent API states
Auth interceptor
JWT refresh flow
interview: Handle loading, empty and error states.
Refactor duplication after the first working version.

topics.title: Frontend System Design
topics.code:
Application
 ├── Core
 │   ├── Auth / HTTP / Config
 │   └── Cross-cutting services
 ├── Shared
 │   └── UI / utilities
 └── Features
     ├── Users
     ├── Orders
     └── Reports
hands: Design a scalable Angular analytics dashboard.
Explain why each state belongs locally, in a facade, or in a centralized store.
interview: How would you scale a component library?
When would Micro Frontends be justified?

topics.title: How to Explain Your Past Projects
theory: Use Problem → Architecture → Responsibility → Challenge → Solution → Result.
Focus on your decisions and trade-offs, not only the technology list.
Be precise about what you personally implemented.
topics.code:
Problem
  ↓
Architecture
  ↓
Your Responsibility
  ↓
Technical Challenge
  ↓
Solution
  ↓
Result
hands: Prepare 3 project stories: dashboard/performance, authentication/RBAC, reusable component architecture.
Prepare one failure/lesson-learned story and one difficult production debugging story.
interview: What was the hardest technical problem?

topics.title: Mock Interview Assessment
hands: Record yourself answering without notes.
After each mock, write the three weakest answers and revisit them.
interview: Can you explain a concept simply?
Can you defend an architecture choice with trade-offs?
